newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors seen arriving at hospital to see Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Doctors seen arriving at hospital to see Yeltsin.

text.p: Top doctors arrived just before noon (0800 GMT) on Wednesday at Russia's Central Clinical Hospital, where they are due to meet President Boris Yeltsin to set a date for his planned heart operation.
Russian heart specialist Yevgeny Chazov arrived in the first car in a convoy of a dozen limousines.

Pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey travelled in another vehicle. Officials have said DeBakey, who conducted the world's first successful heart bypass operation, will advise the Russian team but will not participate in the surgery itself.

Yeltsin, 65, has been in the Central Clinical Hospital since September 13 and aides have said doctors are conducting tests and preparing him for a bypass operation to improve blood supply to the heart.

The Kremlin says the president is in full control of affairs of state, working on documents for up to 2-1/2 hours a day. But Yeltsin's prolonged hospital stay has prompted speculation that he is less fit than the aides have indicated.
Almost 20 television crews waited outside the hospital grounds on Wednesday morning for a glimpse of the medical team.
It is not clear when the specialists will reveal their recommendations, but some members of the medical team have said it could be several days before a decision is made public.

It is not known precisely how many doctors would take part in the council, but Interfax news agency said those definitely to attend were top Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin and head of the Kremlin medical centre Sergei Mironov.

Akchurin, a pupil of DeBakey, is expected to lead the operation. Interfax said in a separate report that Akchurin was likely to fly to Germany after the council meeting to consult some German experts.

Akchurin broke new grounds in a frank television interview at the weekend in which he said Yeltsin may have had a third heart attack between the first and second rounds of voting for Russia's presidential election.
The remarks raised the spectrum that the operation could be cancelled because Yeltsin was not fit to withstand it, but Akchurin on Tuesday ruled this out.
